All is not well in paradise

But does this mean I think Sénégal is some magical place that's kept its communal paradise? No! The warmth has hard limits, and for LGBTQ+ people who cross them, it can be brutal.

Sénégal passed a law in March 2026 (Law No. 2026-08) that increased the penalty for consensual same-sex intimacy to 5 to 10 years in prison, and it also made public "apology" for homosexuality a crime, along with certain financing or support meant to promote it. Homosexuals were already facing arrests, family rejection, harassment, assault and mob violence, but some say they're actually protected once they're arrested, because then at least the mob can't get at them. I can't just praise the virtues of community and ignore the people who have to hide who they are to survive in it, or leave.
